lessons.culture: Taxis in Sana'a and other Yemeni cities are usually hailed on the street or through informal networks. Negotiating the fare before getting in is common, and meters are not always used. Drivers often prefer to agree on a fixed price, and it is normal and polite to do so. Addressing the driver respectfully and bargaining over the fare is part of the culture.

lessons.culture: Public buses and microbuses (minibuses) are very common in Yemen for traveling between cities and within towns. Riders typically agree on the fare with the driver before boarding, and buses depart when they are full rather than on a fixed schedule. Microbuses (mikro) are faster, more informal, and cheaper than full-size buses, and they often stop anywhere along the route.

lessons.culture: In Yemeni cities, important landmarks like mosques, markets, banks, and government buildings serve as reference points for directions. Neighborhoods often have a central square (ساحة) where important buildings are located. Many people know the city by these landmarks rather than by street names or numbers. Visiting restaurants and markets is a social activity where families often gather, especially in the evenings.

exercises.tip: "تاكسي" and "باص" are both borrowed words in Yemeni, like in many other spoken languages.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Will you drop me at the station?" (to a man)

too_formal.item: هل تستطيع أن توصلني إلى المحطة؟
too_formal.feedback: This is formal Arabic; the everyday question is just "توصلني...؟".

exercises.tip: Say the verb with a rising voice; no extra question word is needed.

challenge.title: أُخْتُ تَاكْسِي
challenge.instructions: أَنْتَ سَائِح فِي الصَّنْعَاء وَتَرِيد تَأْجِير تَاكْسِي. تَكَلَّم مَعَ السَّوَّاق عَنِ الْجِهَة الَّتِي تَبِي تَرُوح، كَم الأَجْرَة، وَأَيْن تُرِيد يِنَزِّلَك. اِسْتَخْدِم عَلَى الْأَقَلّ: الْعَدَّاد، الْاتِّجَاه (يَمِين/شِمَال)، الْقِيْمَة، والشُّكْر.

dialogue.speaker: سائح
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَام عَلَيْكُم، أَبِي أَرُوح الْسُّوق الْقَدِيم.
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you, I want to go to the old market.

dialogue.speaker: سواق
dialogue.english: And upon you peace, get in brother.

dialogue.speaker: سائح
dialogue.english: Turn on the meter please.

dialogue.speaker: سواق
dialogue.english: Okay, but the road has a lot of traffic.

dialogue.speaker: سائح
dialogue.english: About how much is the fare?

dialogue.speaker: سواق
dialogue.english: About two thousand riyals brother.

dialogue.speaker: سائح
dialogue.english: Okay, turn right here.

dialogue.speaker: سواق
dialogue.english: Sure, I know the way.

dialogue.speaker: سائح
dialogue.english: Stop here in front of the mosque.

dialogue.speaker: سواق
dialogue.english: Here we are, we've arrived.

dialogue.speaker: سائح
dialogue.english: What's the total?

dialogue.speaker: سواق
dialogue.english: Two thousand one hundred riyals.

dialogue.speaker: سائح
dialogue.english: Here, and keep the change.

dialogue.speaker: سواق
dialogue.english: May God give you health, goodbye.
